item.title: List of African countries that have their own unique calendars
item.description: Several African countries have calendars that are distinct from the Gregorian calendar, either because they maintain traditional systems of dating or because their religious and cultural communities follow their own calendars. The most notable example is Ethiopia, which has a separate calendar system used for official civil purposes. Other countries have indigenous or religious calendars that remain culturally significant, although they are not necessarily used for government administration. African countries with unique calendar systems 1. Ethiopia – Ethiopian (Ge’ez) Calendar Ethiopia operates a calendar that is approximately seven to eight years behind the Gregorian calendar. It has 13 months : 12 months of 30 days and a final month called Pagume, which has five or six days. Its New Year usually falls on September 11. 2. Egypt – Coptic Calendar The Coptic calendar descends from the ancient Egyptian calendar and is still used by the Coptic Orthodox Church. It has 13 months, with 12 months of 30 days and a short 13th month. Its New Year is known as Nayrouz. 3. Eritrea – Ge’ez Calendar Eritrean Orthodox Christians follow the Ge’ez calendar, which is closely related to Ethiopia’s calendar. Its New Year is called Kidus Yohannes and is celebrated around September 11. Eritrea uses the Gregorian calendar for official administration. 4. Morocco – Amazigh (Berber) Calendar The Amazigh calendar is used traditionally by Berber communities. It follows an agricultural year and marks its New Year, Yennayer, around January 12–14. Morocco recognises Yennayer as a public holiday. 5. Algeria – Amazigh Calendar Algeria also observes the Amazigh agricultural calendar. Yennayer marks the beginning of the traditional year and is celebrated as an important cultural occasion. 6. Nigeria – Igbo Traditional Calendar The Igbo calendar, known as Ọgụ́àfọ̀ Ị̀gbò, has 13 months in its traditional structure. Its week consists of four market days: Eke, Orie, Afọ and Nkwọ. It is used in traditional religious, cultural and market activities, although different Igbo communities may calculate it differently. 7. Ghana – Akan Calendar The Akan people use a traditional 42-day cycle known as Adaduanan, combining a six-day week and a seven-day week. It helps determine traditional festivals, ceremonies and important cultural events. Similar practices are found among Akan communities in Côte d’Ivoire. item.title: More than 900 US flights cancelled Sunday after Friday’s ground stop
item.description: …FAA expects flight schedules to recover by late Sunday By Juliet Umeh More than 900 flights scheduled for Sunday in the United States had been cancelled by late Saturday as airlines continued to recover from a nationwide ground stop imposed by the Federal Aviation Administration, FAA. FlightAware, a flight-tracking service, recorded 910 cancellations for Sunday, with the figure rising. More than 6,400 flights were cancelled on Saturday, following about 9,200 on Friday. The FAA order halted nearly all departing flights for almost five hours on Friday. Although it was lifted that evening, passengers continued to face cancellations and delays as airlines worked to reposition aircraft and crews. FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford said, “I do think the worst is behind us,” but added that “a significant amount of recovery work” remained. He apologised to travellers, saying: “I’m sorry that we put you through this, but we did it for the right reasons.” US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the disruption began during work to replace old copper telecommunications lines with fibre-optic cables at an FAA facility. A router involved in the upgrade overloaded parts of the network, affecting air traffic communications and radar systems. “We had over 1,000 connection attempts every four to five seconds,” Duffy said, adding that the surge caused “issues with our communication with airplanes” and disrupted radar feeds. Officials are investigating whether the problem resulted from an installation error or faulty equipment. “We haven’t determined what the fault was,” Duffy said. Bedford said airlines expected to restore their schedules by late Sunday. “Based on everything that we’re hearing from our airline partners, they believe that they’ll be able to have full schedule integrity by the close of business on Sunday,” he said. The FAA said it ordered the ground stop as a safety measure after communications problems affected 17 of its 22 en-route air traffic control centres. Bedford said, “No facilities went dark. Nothing was fully lost.” He also said there was “zero evidence of anything nefarious, and zero evidence of anything AI-related.” The post More than 900 US flights cancelled Sunday after Friday’s ground stop appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: NDLEA arrests American basketballer over 34kg cannabis consignment
item.description: Operatives of the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) have intercepted a 25.05 kilograms consignment of methamphetamine at the Murtala Muhammed International Airport (MMIA), Ikeja, Lagos. The agency’s Director, Media and Advocacy, Mr Femi Babafemi, disclosed this in a statement on Sunday in Abuja. Babafemi said that the drugs were concealed in packs of assorted breakfast cereals imported from South Africa. He said that the NDLEA operatives arrested the 56-year-old trafficker who had lived in South Africa for over two decades under a stolen identity. He added that the meth suspect was arrested on Wednesday at the arrival hall of Terminal II of the Lagos airport upon his return from South Africa. “A thorough search of his two travelling boxes led to the recovery of twenty-five parcels of a white crystalline substance, which tested positive for methamphetamine with a total weight of 25.05kg. “The parcels had been carefully concealed inside packs of assorted breakfast cereals and cereal-based food products in a bid to beat security screening. “The 56-year-old suspect holds both Nigerian and South African passports and has been resident in South Africa for over 24 years. “During preliminary interview, he confessed that he adopted the fake Nigerian name after using forged documents to gain entry into South Africa and had continued to use that identity ever since. “He further stated that he was contracted by a South Africa-based man to deliver the illicit consignment in Nigeria for a fee of R20,000,”he said. Babafemi further disclosed that the agency’s operatives at the same airport, arrested an American professional basketball player over a 33.95kg shipment of Loud, a potent strain of cannabis, from Thailand. Babafemi said that on Wednesday, acting on credible intelligence, NDLEA operatives at the MMIA intercepted a 28-year-old American citizen who arrived in Lagos aboard an Emirates Airline flight from Thailand via Dubai. He said that the suspect, who was placed under discreet surveillance upon arrival, was observed abandoning his two checked-in bags before attempting to exit the airport with only his carry-on luggage. “He was promptly apprehended at the airport car park. “A search of the two abandoned bags, both bearing his name tag, revealed sixteen parcels of Loud in each, totalling thirty-two parcels with a combined weight of 33.95 kilograms. “A tracking device was also recovered from the bags. The suspect, a native of Savannah, Georgia, USA, claimed he has lived in Thailand since October 2025 where he plays professional basketball. “The suspect said he came to Nigeria on holiday to build networks for his basketball career. “A forensic examination of his mobile phone revealed information pointing to his knowledge of and involvement in the drug trafficking activity,”he said The post NDLEA arrests American basketballer over 34kg cannabis consignment appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Revenue leakages: FG to deploy export automation system as non-oil sector hits over $6b
item.description: By Daniel Abia P/Harcourt The Federal Government has concluded the process to deploy an automated export processing system to strengthen regulatory compliance and curb revenue leakages in the exports sector. This was disclosed by, Mr Tola Fakolade, the Project Director, National Single Window (NSW), at the Phase Two Export Sensitization Joint Stakeholders Engagement in Port Harcourt on Thursday. The event had as its theme, “Unlocking Endless Possibilities: A Comprehensive Outlook on the NSW Project”. Fakolade described the NSW as a Federal Government initiative designed to streamline international trade through a unified digital platform for trade documentation, permits and approvals. “The second phase of the project, scheduled to commence on Dec. 14, is expected to eliminate the multiple bottlenecks, delays and revenue leakages that have long frustrated exporters,” he said. He said the first batch of the phase would cover the issuance of export permit issuance by agencies, including the Standards Organisation of Nigeria (SON), NAFDAC and Federal Produce Inspection Service. According to him, the second batch, involving processes handled by the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN), would commence in the first quarter of 2027. Fakolade explained that the first phase had streamlined the submission of licences and permits by integrating the digital systems of various regulatory agencies. He said the platform had also strengthened compliance by ensuring that users met regulatory requirements before accessing relevant services. “One of the testimonials we received from agencies during the first phase was that enforced compliance on the platform helped users comply with regulations. “When there is compliance, there is also a reduction in revenue leakages,” he said. The NSW project director said the project team was engaging exporters and other stakeholders nationwide to ensure adequate awareness ahead of the second phase. He listed Enugu, Akure, Jos, Lagos and Port Harcourt among the cities already visited, adding that sensitisation would continue in Kano and Abuja. He said the NSW team was collaborating with the Nigerian Export Promotion Council (NEPC), which maintains the database of registered exporters. “The partnership would provide access to relevant information and insights required for effective implementation of the export phase,” he said. Fakolade said the project had completed its User Acceptance Testing and would commence end-user training on Monday. He urged exporters and other stakeholders to register for the training to familiarise themselves with the platform ahead of its implementation. Meanwhile,Mrs Nonye Ayeni, the Executive Director of the Nigerian Export Promotion Council (NEPC), said Nigeria’s non-oil export earnings rose by 11.5 per cent to 6.1 billion dollars (N875.4 billion) in 2025. item.title: Stop weaponising public for political relevance – Obi’s media office to Wike, Keyamo
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA- THE Media Office of the Presidential Candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC ahead of January 16 2027 election, Peter Obi has taken a swipe at the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory Administration, FCTA, Nyesom Wike and the Minister Nigeria’s Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, SAN, over attacks on the Presidential candidate over National anthem. In a statement signed on Sunday by the Spokesperson of Peter Obi Media Reach, POMR, Idris Zekeri, he described them as rabble rousers, warning them to stop weaponising public for political relevance. According to Zekeri, a government minister is not a political warlord and public office is neither a private arsenal nor are Nigeria’s state institutions extensions of any politician’s personal political organisation, urging Wike and Keyamo to recognise that they hold their offices in trust for Nigerians, not to serve political egos or protect partisan interests, adding that even more concerning is the attempt to portray partisan conduct as patriotism. The statement read, ” the Peter Obi Media Office strongly condemns the disturbing conduct of Ministers Nyesom Wike and Festus Keyamo, who appear to be exploiting their official positions for partisan political confrontation, treating the authority entrusted to them by Nigerians as though it were personal property to be deployed against political opponents. Their conduct raises a fundamental question: when did public service become an instrument for political intimidation, personal vendettas and the pursuit of narrow partisan interests? ” A government minister is not a political warlord. Public office is neither a private arsenal nor are Nigeria’s state institutions extensions of any politician’s personal political organisation. Wike and Keyamo must recognise that they hold their offices in trust for Nigerians, not to serve political egos or protect partisan interests. Even more concerning is the attempt to portray partisan conduct as patriotism. “Patriotism is not measured by the forcefulness of political rhetoric, the harshness of attacks on opponents or the unconditional defence of a government. It is demonstrated by service, integrity, respect for the rule of law and an unwavering commitment to the welfare of citizens. Claims of patriotism should be subjected to careful scrutiny rather than accepted without question. Nigerians must differentiate political antagonism from genuine patriotism and understand that loyalty to a political establishment is not equivalent to commitment to the nation. “No individual or political organisation has an exclusive monopoly on patriotism. item.title: Cabo Verde Votes In Presidential Election As Incumbent Seeks Second Term
item.description: Cabo Verde voted for a new president on Sunday, with incumbent Jose Maria Neves favoured to win a second term as head of state of the West African archipelago renowned for its democratic stability. He is facing the country’s first woman candidate, Joana Rosa Amado, among other contenders. Voting started at 0900 GMT and ends at 1900 GMT. Provisional results are expected overnight. “I’ve voted. Now I’m going to mass, and I believe everything will go well — normally and with civic-mindedness,” Adilia Gomes, 55, told AFP after casting her ballot in the capital, Praia. “Everything went normally despite a few minutes’ delay in the opening of my polling station,” added another voter, Claudino Semedo. Nearly 420,000 people are eligible to vote. The election is being watched by about 150 observers from the Economic Community of West African States, the African Union and European Union. A supporter of Cape Verde’s President and presidential candidate Jose Maria Neves waves a flag bearing his image during a campaign rally in Mindelo, on the island of Sao Vicente, on October 30, 2026.(Photo by QUEILA FERNANDES / AFP) Cabo Verde, located in the Atlantic Ocean about 600 kilometres (375 miles) off the coast of Senegal, comprises 10 volcanic islands and is an increasingly popular tourist destination. It made world headlines this year when its national football team reached the knockout stages in its first World Cup, and when a cruise ship containing people with hantavirus docked off its shores. Stability, Hospitality Unlike several of its West African neighbours where presidential elections have been tense in recent years, Cabo Verde is known for its political stability and good governance. It is considered a model of democracy in Africa, with strong economic growth. A voter queues at a polling station during Cape Verde’s presidential election in Mindelo, on the island of Sao Vicente, on November 15, 2026(Photo by QUEILA FERNANDES / AFP) The country is known for its “morabeza” (“hospitality”, in local creole), openness, and carnivals. It also has its own style of music. According to the Mo Ibrahim Foundation 2026 index on global governance, Cabo Verde ranks third out of 54 countries on the continent. Politically, it has a semi-presidential system in which the executive is dominated by the prime minister. The president does not govern but acts more as an arbiter, working to guarantee unity and uphold the constitution. The head of state appoints the prime minister based on the results of legislative elections and represents the country abroad. item.title: Meta fined €805m for accessing users’ photos, videos without consent
item.description: Italian regulators fined Facebook parent company Meta 805 million euros ($880 million) for accessing users’ photos without their “specific” consent, the country’s data protection authority said on Saturday. Through the Facebook application for Android devices, Meta accessed photographs, videos and related metadata belonging to Italian users “without obtaining specific consent and without properly informing them”, the authority said in a statement. Meta said it would appeal the decision. A company spokesperson said “we strongly disagree” with the assessment by the regulators “and the disproportionate level of the fine”. In late October, authorities in New Mexico ordered Meta to pay $25 billion for having misled the state’s residents for more than a decade over use of their data — a record fine for the company, which slammed it as a “tax” on freedom of expression. Saturday’s latest fine is among the largest an Italian authority has ever imposed on a tech giant. In 2021, Amazon received a more than 1.1-billion-euro fine for breaching competition law. That sum was subsequently reduced to 752 million euros on appeal. – Facebook gallery feature – The Italian penalty imposed on Facebook relates to its gallery suggestions feature, available since 2023, which suggests photos and videos from a user’s phone gallery as ideas for posts as they are browsing. According to Italy’s regulator, Facebook requested access to the gallery via a single authorisation valid for the entire app, preceded by a generic notice requesting enabling of other features, which did not allow users to understand that they were also authorising suggestions from their gallery. The regulator said Meta would now have to seek consent by means of a separate and specific request for the feature concerned and clearly signpost what it is used for, namely that it involves access to a user’s photo gallery, as well as how to disable it. In determining the size of the fine, the authority said it took into account “the high number of people affected” — around 20 million Android users in Italy — and the duration of the infringement, “which is still ongoing for those who have not updated the app and for those who have already given their consent to the system”. The authority also cited “Meta’s lack of cooperation during the investigation”. It imposed a fine amounting to roughly 0.4 per cent of the group’s annual turnover, which hit $201 billion in 2025, for a net profit of $60.5 billion. item.title: Hold APC responsible if anything happens to Nigeria’s democracy — Wabara
item.description: . Rejects Appeal Court ruling on PDP leadership crisis . Warns against making Tinubu sole presidential candidate By Steve Oko UMUAHIA – Former Senate President and Chairman of the Board of Trustees (BoT) of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), Senator Adolphus Wabara, has warned the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) to accept responsibility should Nigerias democracy suffer any setback arising from what he described as the systematic weakening of opposition parties. Wabara, who expressed strong reservations over the recent Court of Appeal judgment in the PDP leadership dispute, accused the ruling party of benefiting from the protracted crises in opposition parties and warned that attempts to weaken political alternatives ahead of the 2027 general elections could undermine Nigeria’s democratic foundations. He described the appellate court’s refusal to compel the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to recognise his faction’s position as a travesty of justice, insisting that the circumstances surrounding the emergence of the Alhaji Abdulrahman Muhammad-led faction raised serious questions about democracy in Nigeria. The former Senate President warned that accepting the Muhammad-led faction’s position without adequately addressing the issues surrounding its emergence amounted to “standing truth in the head”. The Court of Appeal, in a unanimous decision by a three-member panel, had declined to disturb the July 17, 2026 judgment of the Federal High Court in Abuja, which dismissed the suit filed by the Wabara-led BoT faction. The appellate court held that the trial judge, Justice Salim Ibrahim, was right to dismiss the suit seeking to validate actions taken on behalf of the PDP by the Tanimu Turaki, SAN-led faction. Those actions included a national convention organised by the faction, which subsequently announced former President Goodluck Jonathan as its consensus presidential candidate for the 2027 election. In the lead judgment delivered virtually by Justice R. O. Ayoola, the appellate court held that the Wabara-led group lacked the locus standi to institute the action on behalf of the PDP. It consequently struck out the party’s name as the eighth appellant and held that the appeal had become academic and amounted to an abuse of judicial process. Reacting to the judgment, Wabara expressed bewilderment at what he described as its questionable legal reasoning, wondering how the appellate court arrived at what he called an inverted interpretation of the issues before it. He cautioned the judiciary against becoming entangled in political disputes in ways that could further erode public confidence in the institution. item.title: Two dead as car fleeing police crashes in UK
item.description: By Juliet Umeh Two people have died after a car being pursued by police collided with their vehicle in Leeds, a city in West Yorkshire in northern England, UK. According to a report, West Yorkshire Police said a blue BMW 123D “failed to stop” for a police vehicle on Gelderd Road at 12:44 a.m. on Sunday. Officers began a pursuit, during which the BMW collided with a white Volkswagen Scirocco turning into Gelderd Road from Lowfields Road. The media report said that the driver of the Volkswagen, a 22-year-old man from York, died at the scene. It said: “His passenger, a 23-year-old woman, also from York, died in hospital a short time later. “A 39-year-old man from Harrogate, who was in the BMW, was arrested on suspicion of causing death by dangerous driving and driving while over the prescribed limit for cannabis. He remains in custody. “Three other occupants of the BMW – two boys aged 16 and 17, and a 16-year-old girl – were taken to hospital with injuries police said were not life-threatening. They have also been arrested on suspicion of causing death by dangerous driving. “The Independent Office for Police Conduct has declared an independent investigation after a referral from West Yorkshire Police. “Gelderd Road remained closed, with drivers advised to avoid the area and use alternative routes,” the report added. The post Two dead as car fleeing police crashes in UK appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Nigeria, Saudi Arabia to begin direct Abuja-Jeddah flights in December, says envoy
item.description: Nigeria and Saudi Arabia are set to strengthen their air connectivity, with Saudi Arabia’s national carrier, Saudia Airlines, scheduled to begin direct flights between Abuja and Jeddah in December. Nigerian Ambassador to Saudi Arabia, Dr Yakubu Gambo, disclosed this in an interview with the News Agency of Nigeria on Sunday. Gambo said the service would subsequently extend to Lagos and Port Harcourt. He said Kano would retain its existing direct flight arrangement, while additional routes were expected to be operational before the end of the first quarter of 2027. “By December, we will start having Saudi air flights directly from Abuja. And it will scale up to Lagos, Port Harcourt and Kano,” he said. Gambo said the arrangement followed adjustments and engagements with Saudi aviation authorities, who expressed willingness to support direct air connectivity between both countries. He said Saudi Arabia had also indicated readiness to provide technical and financial support for Nigeria to operate flights through its national carrier. According to him, the arrangement will enable Nigerian pilgrims travelling for Hajj and Umrah to fly directly between both countries without transiting through other territories. “They wouldn’t want pilgrims coming for Umrah or Hajj to fly through other territories that may not be safe,” he said. The ambassador said President Bola Tinubu had been briefed on the proposal and welcomed the initiative. He confirmed that direct flights would also be available for Nigerian pilgrims during the 2027 Hajj exercise. The post Nigeria, Saudi Arabia to begin direct Abuja-Jeddah flights in December, says envoy appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2027: Okpebholo’s 2.5m votes for Tinubu achievable says Afegbua
item.description: By Ozioruva Aliu BENIN CITY – THE Edo State Commissioner for Information and Strategy, Hon. Kassim Afegbua, on Sunday defended Governor Monday Okpebholo’s pledge to deliver 2.5 million votes for President Bola Tinubu in the 2027 presidential election, describing the figure as a target achievable through massive voter mobilisation and the state government’s development projects. Afegbua, who spoke on Arise Television’s Sunday morning programme, monitored in Benin City, said the target was based on the state’s growing voter population. He said that the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) had put Edo’s eligible voters at 2.865 million. The commissioner said the state government was determined to mobilise, sensitise and persuade voters to support Tinubu’s re-election, arguing that the administration’s infrastructure and social development projects had provided reasons for the people to endorse the President. He said, “The context at which we made that statement is the fact that we are setting a target for ourselves. After all, the new voters, as at last week when INEC released the figures, is 2.865 million people. What happens if we get 2.5 million? Is it a crime? “We are doing so much, we are working so much, we are building infrastructure, we are touching the social development aspect, we are building schools, health sectors, and all of that,” he said. Afegbua added that the government’s responsibility was to convince Edo voters to support Tinubu for another term, particularly because of the increased federal allocations to states. He said, “Our responsibility is to woo them, plead with them, appeal to them that they should allow the man who is providing the funding with respect to increase allocation to the state to continue so that they can see more development. “It is even dangerous for economic growth of any country for you to disrupt the flow or the process as it were now, when things are getting stabilised,” Afegbua said, adding that Edo was ready to deliver Tinubu in 2027. The commissioner disclosed that Okpebholo was expected to begin a tour of the state’s 192 polling wards to canvass support for the President, stressing that the government would work to ensure voters were mobilised and their votes counted. “Edo people are ready. We are going to deliver Edo State to President Tinubu, and we are very proud of it, and we are going to work assiduously,” he said. Afegbua also defended the Director-General of Tinubu’s Presidential Campaign Council, former Zamfara State Governor, Abdulaziz Yari, over his remark that Nigerians could still go to the market and find food to buy, urging a holistic interpretation of the statement. item.title: Tinubu’s economic reforms need continuity beyond 2027 – Jigawa Gov
item.description: By Muhammad Inuwa, Dutse ‎ ‎Jigawa State Governor, Malam Umar Namadi, has urged Nigerians to sustain President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s administration beyond 2027, saying the ongoing economic reforms require continuity to deliver their intended benefits to citizens. ‎ ‎Namadi made the appeal on Saturday during the flag-off of the 2027 presidential, governorship and other elective positions campaign for the Jigawa North-West Senatorial District in Gumel. ‎ ‎The governor called on voters to support the All Progressives Congress (APC) candidates at all levels, from the presidency to the State House of Assembly, to ensure the continuation of policies and reforms introduced by the Tinubu administration. ‎ ‎He said the country needed to sustain the ongoing economic reforms so that their benefits could translate into improved livelihoods and greater economic opportunities for ordinary Nigerians. ‎ ‎Namadi particularly highlighted Tinubu’s agricultural reforms, saying the President was determined to make farming profitable again by ensuring that farmers earned meaningful income from their hard work. ‎ ‎”President Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu said farming must pay again. Not just hard work, but money in your pocket. That is the agricultural reform he is championing, and Jigawa will benefit from it,” he said. ‎ ‎He also urged residents of Jigawa North-West Senatorial District to give the APC another mandate in 2027, arguing that continuity would enable the party to consolidate its achievements and complete ongoing reforms. ‎ ‎Speaking on his administration’s performance, Namadi said his government had recorded significant achievements since assuming office in 2023. ‎ ‎Meanwhile, the APC Chairman in Jigawa State, Ahmad Garba, has declared that the party remains open to receiving members of opposition parties willing to defect ahead of the 2027 general elections. ‎ ‎Garba stated this while receiving 1,514 defectors from the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) during the zonal campaign rally in Gumel. ‎ ‎He said the party was ready to accommodate politicians and supporters from other political parties who identified with its leadership, programmes and political direction. ‎ ‎The APC chairman expressed confidence that the party’s achievements under Governor Namadi would continue to attract more supporters, urging members to remain united and intensify grassroots mobilisation ahead of the elections. ‎ ‎Speaking on behalf of the defectors, Malam Tijjani said the 1,514 members drawn from the 11 wards of Gumel Local Government Area joined the APC because of its people-oriented policies and programmes. ‎ ‎He assured the party leadership that the new members were prepared to work towards its victory in the 2027 general elections. ‎ The post Tinubu’s economic reforms need continuity beyond 2027 – Jigawa Gov appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: UK tells Nigerian woman after 26 years to wait 20 more years for settlement
item.description: A 67-year-old blind Nigerian woman who has lived in the United Kingdom for 26 years has been told she may have to wait another 20 years before qualifying for permanent residency under proposed changes to the country’s immigration settlement rules. The woman, identified as Comfort, arrived in the UK in 2000 but lost her sight shortly afterwards after developing acute glaucoma. After spending 20 years in the country, she was granted permission to remain in 2022 under the long-residence immigration route. Under the arrangement, migrants are required to renew their visas every 30 months for 10 years before becoming eligible to apply for indefinite leave to remain, which allows them to live permanently in the UK. However, following new settlement rules announced by Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood, Comfort is likely to face an additional 20-year wait before qualifying for permanent residency, meaning she could be in her 80s by the time she becomes eligible. Concerned about her age and disability, lawyers at Refugee and Migrant Justice applied to the Home Office for her to be granted indefinite leave to remain immediately under provisions that allow exceptional cases to be fast-tracked. The application was rejected, with the Home Office initially telling her that she could return to Nigeria because services for blind people were available there. However, the refusal letter concluded: “Your circumstances are not so severe or lacking in potential treatment in India that it would warrant indefinite leave to remain in this case.” Comfort expressed disappointment over the decision, saying she had established her life in the UK and had no connection with India. “In 2022, I got my permission to stay here based on long residence in the UK,” she said. “I’m very disheartened that I may now need to wait nearly 20 years to get indefinite leave to remain. “I have been living in this country for 26 years. I have found my home here and settled well. I have my friends, my church and do voluntary work. I’m a good citizen, not a law-breaker and am begging the Home Office to have mercy on me and grant me indefinite leave to remain now, rather than making me wait 20 more years. “I don’t know why the Home Office said I could go back to India. It’s a country I have never visited and have no connection with.” Nick Beales, head of campaigning at Migrant and Refugee Justice, who is supporting Comfort, criticised the government’s handling of the case and the proposed changes to settlement rules. “This woman is blind, in her late 60s and has lived in the UK for a quarter of a century. She meets the rules to remain here and there is no public interest in making her continue to renew her visa. “Rather than viewing these vulnerable people as human beings, the government is fixated on appearing tough. item.title: NDLEA intercepts meth consignments from South Africa, hidden in cereals packs
item.description: **Arrest American Professional Basketball Player over Shipment of Loud. **Busts Gun Factory in Kaduna, Nabs Woman with 196 AK-47 Ammunition **Seizes Tons of Illicit Drugs After Raids in Lagos, Ondo, Delta, Edo, Osun. By: Kingsley Omonobi Fhe National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) said on Sunday that it’s operatives have intercepted 25.05 kilograms consignment of methamphetamine concealed in packs of assorted breakfast cereals imported from South Africa through the Murtala Muhammed International Airport (MMIA), Ikeja, Lagos, and arrested the 56-year-old trafficker who has lived in South Africa for over two decades under a stolen identity. In another interception at the same airport, an American professional basketball player was arrested over a 33.95kg shipment of Loud, a potent strain of cannabis, from Thailand, while a factory producing illegal firearms was busted in Kaduna while tons of assorted illicit substances were seized in raids across Lagos, Ondo, Delta, Edo and Osun states. Spokesman of the agency, Femi Babafemi said the meth suspect, Omokan Isaac Babatope, whose real name is Chinedu Onwude, was arrested on Wednesday 11th November 2026 at the arrival hall of Terminal II of the Lagos airport upon his return from South Africa. “A thorough search of his two travelling boxes led to the recovery of twenty-five parcels of a white crystalline substance, which tested positive for methamphetamine with a total weight of 25.05kg. “The parcels had been carefully concealed inside packs of assorted breakfast cereals and cereal-based food products in a bid to beat security screening. “The 56-year-old suspect holds both Nigerian and South African passports and has been resident in South Africa for over 24 years. “During preliminary interview, he confessed that he adopted the name Omokan Isaac Babatope after using forged documents to gain entry into South Africa and had continued to use that identity ever since. “He further stated that he was contracted by a South Africa-based man, Obiora Okoye, to deliver the illicit consignment in Nigeria for a fee of Twenty Thousand South African Rands (R20,000). Also, on Wednesday 11th November, acting on credible intelligence, NDLEA operatives at the MMIA intercepted a 28-year-old American citizen, Greene Da’monte Khiree, who arrived in Lagos aboard an Emirates Airline flight from Thailand via Dubai. The suspect, who was placed under discreet surveillance upon arrival, was observed abandoning his two checked-in bags before attempting to exit the airport with only his carry-on luggage. He was promptly apprehended at the airport car park. A search of the two abandoned bags, both bearing his name tag, revealed sixteen parcels of Loud in each, totalling thirty-two parcels with a combined weight of 33.95 kilograms. A tracking device was also recovered from the bags. item.title: Fela, Queen Latifah, Phil Collins Join Rock Hall Of Fame
item.description: Afrobeat pioneer Fela Kuti, rhapsodic hip-hop transformers Wu-Tang Clan and punk rocker Billy Idol were among the music luminaries inducted Saturday into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame at a star-studded concert gala. The versatile Phil Collins, post-punk and electronic dance music renegades Joy Division/New Order, and the velvet-voiced late Luther Vandross also joined the rock pantheon at the ceremony held in Los Angeles’s Peacock Theater. But several of the 2026 class of artists — Oasis, Sade and Iron Maiden — skipped the night celebrating their honor, one of the music industry’s most prestigious. But the show went on. Staten Island’s own Wu-Tang Clan — the ragtag group of New Yorkers who paired raw production with streetwise rhymes and martial arts influences — brought the ruckus, performing their own hits including “C.R.E.A.M” and “Wu‐Tang Clan Ain’t Nuthing ta F’ Wit.” “We went from being banned on the radio to the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame,” said member Method Man onstage to resounding cheers. To the haters, he said, “you can kiss my inducted ass.” It proved a banner night for women in hip-hop, with honorees including Queen Latifah as well as MC Lyte, who is widely recognized as the “First Lady of Hip Hop.” The storied performers tore up the stage with a medley of their hits, before Megan Thee Stallion and Remy Ma joined them to underscore the legacy of women in rap. Travis Barker, the drummer from Blink-182, inducted Collins, drawing tears from the British artist who attended the ceremony alongside his children, including Lily of “Emily in Paris” fame. US rapper/actress Queen Latifah attends the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame Induction Ceremony at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles on November 14, 2026. (Photo by VALERIE MACON / AFP) Collins — whose entry into the hall is his second, the first was as part of the band Genesis — walked to the stage with two canes, taking the mic and saying, “I’m really not as bad as it looks.” “You haven’t heard the last of me, I can promise you that.” Cynthia Erivo belted out Collins’s smash “In The Air Tonight,” with Barker playing the instantly recognizable drum fill. “My life has just been one thing after the other, one dream after the other,” Collins said to journalists backstage. item.title: 2027: SERAP Gives INEC Seven Days To Prosecute Electoral Violence Suspects
item.description: The Socio-Economic Rights and Accountability Project (SERAP) has given the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) seven days to prosecute persons arrested over reported incidents of electoral and political violence ahead of the 2027 general elections or face legal action. SERAP made the demand in a letter dated November 14, 2026, and addressed to INEC Chairman, Professor Joash Amupitan, urging the commission to obtain relevant case files and investigation materials from the Nigeria Police Force and prosecute suspects where sufficient evidence exists. The organisation also asked INEC to direct its legal officers or appointed legal practitioners to review the files and promptly initiate prosecutions under the Electoral Act 2026. The demand follows several reported incidents of political violence across the country since campaigns for the 2027 elections began on 19 August, including the latest attack on members and supporters of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) during a town hall meeting in Oregun, Lagos, on 12 November. In the letter signed by its Deputy Director, Kolawole Oluwadare, SERAP urged Amupitan to press the police to conclude investigations into other reported attacks, arrest suspected perpetrators and their sponsors, and forward relevant evidence to INEC. It also called on the commission to exercise its powers under Section 83 of the Electoral Act 2026 to demand explanations from political parties suspected of involvement in or encouraging prohibited conduct and impose prescribed fines on those that fail to comply with lawful directives. SERAP expressed concern over reports of attacks on political convoys, party secretariats, rallies and meetings, as well as intimidation of candidates and supporters. Cited incidents included the reported obstruction of the convoy of NDC presidential candidate Peter Obi in Benue State on 8 September; attacks on political meetings in Enugu State on 12 September; and the attack on the convoy of ADC senatorial candidate Herberta Okonofua in Edo State on 6 October. Others included attacks on supporters of Accord governorship candidate Oriyomi Hamzat in Ibadan on 14 October, which reportedly resulted in one death, and the attack on the convoy of NDC candidate Rollins Offia-Nwali in Ebonyi State on 22 October, which allegedly left one person dead and three injured. The organisation also cited the reported attack on African Action Congress (AAC) presidential candidate Omoyele Sowore and his team in Ado-Ekiti on 30 October, the attack on Obi’s convoy in Calabar on 4 November, and an NDC procession in Asaba on 7 November, which reportedly left one person dead and five injured. It added that journalist Samuel Adebanjo was assaulted and his equipment seized while covering the November 12 incident in Lagos. item.title: Former APC spokesman warns of crisis if Tinubu is imposed in 2027
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: Former Deputy National Publicity Secretary of the ruling All Progressives Congress APC, Timi Frank, has warned that any attempt to force President Bola Tinubu back into office in 2027 could plunge the country into crisis. Frank, who is the Ambassador to East Africa and the Middle East of the United Liberation Movement for West Papua (ULMWP), said Nigerians would not accept an outcome that contradicts their votes. “Nigerians will not accept a situation in which someone is declared the winner when the people know they did not vote for him. They should not push the country into a crisis by attempting to impose him on the people,” Frank warned. He urged the president to abandon his re-election ambition and guarantee a transparent electoral process. “Whoever wins should be allowed to emerge as the choice of the people,” he said. Frank also expressed concern over alleged attempts by some political actors to manipulate the electoral process. He described the public protest against Tinubu after prayers at the Shehu Shagari Mosque in Area 1, Garki, Abuja, last Friday as evidence of growing dissatisfaction with the administration. Tinubu reportedly faced boos from some Hausa protesters who chanted “Ba ma yi” (we don’t want you) after the prayers. In a viral video, some protesters were seen removing and destroying his campaign posters and billboards in parts of Area 1. Frank condemned the protesters for choosing a religious occasion to vent their displeasure and commended the President’s security detail for ensuring his safety and de-escalating the situation. He nevertheless urged the President to recognise the significance of the public reaction. “The rejection was total and unmistakable. No Nigerian president has been embarrassed like this publicly. The way Nigerians rejected him speaks volumes but should he decide to go ahead and he loses, he should be prepared to accept defeat just like former President Goodluck Jonathan did,” he said. The former APC spokesman said he was worried by what he called a growing gap between the assurances given to the President by political associates and the mood of the people. “I have seen the confidence with which some people are assuring President Tinubu that he will win the Federal Capital Territory FCT and that he is firmly in control. But the reported embarrassment he suffered during a prayer session in Abuja tells a different story. “What happened in the FCT last Friday showed that political assurances and promises are not necessarily a reflection of the reality on the ground. item.title: NGE demands release of detained investigative journalist, Ojukwu
item.description: The Nigerian Guild of Editors (NGE) has condemned the arrest, detention and prosecution of Daniel Ojukwu, an investigative journalist with the Foundation for Investigative Journalism (FIJ), demanding his immediate release on bail. The Guild also called for a review of the criminal charges against Ojukwu and FIJ founder, Fisayo Soyombo, warning that the prosecution could undermine press freedom and discourage investigative journalism in Nigeria. Ojukwu is currently being held at the Kuje Correctional Centre, Abuja, after being arraigned on a 12-count charge bordering on alleged cyberstalking and criminal defamation. In a statement dated November 15 and signed by its President, Eze Anaba, and General Secretary, Onuoha Ukeh, the NGE said it was alarmed that a journalist was facing criminal prosecution over reports raising questions about the expenditure of public funds by the Office of the Senior Special Assistant to the President on Sustainable Development Goals. The Guild said Ojukwu’s investigation reportedly exposed an alleged payment of more than ₦147 million, approximately $109,000, to an Abuja-based restaurant for the construction of classrooms and a skills acquisition centre at a primary school in Lagos. According to the NGE, the investigation raised questions about the existence of the projects, as well as the capacity and track record of the company involved in the contract. It described the issues raised by the investigation as legitimate matters of public accountability that deserved transparent answers rather than the prosecution of the journalist who brought them to public attention. The Guild expressed particular concern that Ojukwu had been remanded in prison despite pleading not guilty to the charges, while his bail application, initially scheduled for November 12, was adjourned until December 1. It said the resort to arrest, detention and criminal prosecution over journalistic work raised concerns about the commitment of authorities to press freedom, freedom of expression and Nigerians’ constitutional right to information. The NGE recalled its opposition to the alleged use of cybersecurity laws by the police and other security agencies to harass, intimidate and bully journalists. “Investigative journalism is not a crime. Asking questions about public expenditure is not cyberstalking. Demanding accountability from public officials is not defamation,” the Guild said. It maintained that public office holders must be open to scrutiny over their management of public resources, adding that journalists should not face threats of arrest, prosecution or imprisonment for reporting alleged irregularities. While acknowledging the right of individuals to seek legal redress over publications they consider injurious to their reputation, the Guild warned against using such rights to intimidate journalists or suppress legitimate investigations. item.title: AFCON 2027: 6 countries who need a win to keep qualification hopes alive
item.description: Six countries are facing an uphill battle to qualify for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) after losing all three of their opening matches in the qualifying campaign. Lesotho, South Sudan, Somalia, Sierra Leone, Central African Republic and Liberia are yet to record a point after three rounds of matches, leaving them bottom of their respective groups . With three matchdays remaining, the six countries will need to turn their fortunes around quickly to stand a realistic chance of securing a place at the tournament. Lesotho occupy the bottom position in Group A after suffering three consecutive defeats. Their latest setback came against Gabon, who secured a 2-0 victory on Friday, November 13. The result left Lesotho without a point, while group leaders Morocco maintained their perfect record with a 5-1 victory over Niger to move to nine points. South Sudan are experiencing a similarly difficult campaign in Group B, having lost their third consecutive match following a 2-0 defeat to Angola on Saturday, November 14. The South Sudanese side are bottom of the group with zero points, eight behind joint leaders Egypt and Angola, who have both collected seven points. In Group C, Somalia are also struggling after losing 2-0 to Ghana on Thursday, November 12. The defeat marked their third straight loss, leaving them at the bottom without a point. Ivory Coast lead the group with nine points after beating Gambia 2-1, while Gambia remain second with six points. Sierra Leone are another country under pressure after losing all three of their opening fixtures in Group E. Their latest defeat came against DR Congo, who secured a 3-1 victory on Thursday, November 12, to maintain their position at the top of the group with nine points. Zimbabwe and Equatorial Guinea occupy second and third positions with four points each, while Sierra Leone remain bottom without a point. Central African Republic have also endured a disappointing start to their qualifying campaign in Group F. They suffered a heavy 4-1 defeat to Benin on Thursday, November 12, leaving them with three losses from three matches. Benin and Burkina Faso are joint leaders of the group with seven points each, while Mauritania occupy third position with three points. Liberia complete the list of six winless countries after losing 4-2 to Cape Verde on Friday, November 13. The defeat left Liberia bottom of Group K without a point, while Mali lead the group with nine points following their 3-2 victory over Rwanda. Rwanda are second with six points, while Cape Verde have three. Although the six countries have made difficult starts, none has been mathematically eliminated from the qualification race, with three rounds of matches still to be played. The fourth round of qualifiers begins on November 16, giving the struggling teams another opportunity to secure their first points and revive their campaigns. item.title: Iran attacks US military base in Bahrain
item.description: Explosions rocked Bahrain early Sunday as Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said it had launched a drone attack on a United States military base in the Gulf nation. The attack came amid renewed hostilities in the Middle East, with Bahrain experiencing fresh Iranian strikes after a lull in attacks. Sirens sounded across the country, while authorities issued several emergency alerts on social media, urging residents to seek shelter. The warnings were the first since September. Bahrain, which hosts a major US naval base, has now been targeted twice in three days. The country’s military said it intercepted several Iranian attacks, preventing them from reaching their intended targets, while the Foreign Ministry confirmed that air defence systems had shot down Iranian drones. Explosions were heard around 4:00 a.m. (0100 GMT), according to an AFP journalist, while residents reported another series of blasts around 6:30 a.m. In a post on X, Bahrain’s Interior Ministry urged residents to remain calm, move to the nearest safe location and follow updates through official channels. Iran’s Revolutionary Guards said their Aerospace Force carried out the attack on a US radar system at a military installation in Bahrain. “The US air defence radar system at the Al-Riffa helicopter base in Bahrain was targeted by six drones belonging to the IRGC Aerospace Force,” the Guards said in a statement carried by Iranian state television and posted on Telegram. “The Strait of Hormuz is closed, and any aggression by the American enemy will be met with an even harsher and more forceful response,” the statement added. Iran has restricted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, a major global oil transit route, during more than eight months of war, while targeting infrastructure including airports, seaports, energy facilities and US assets across the region. Bahrain condemns attacks Bahrain is among the Gulf countries that have faced thousands of Iranian drone and missile strikes since the conflict began on February 28. In a statement, the country’s Foreign Ministry rejected the use of its territory as a battleground in the conflict and held Iran responsible for the attacks and their consequences. Bahrain “rejects turning its territory into an arena for settling scores and holds Iran fully responsible for these attacks and their consequences,” the ministry said. On Friday, the Revolutionary Guards had announced that they targeted a US early-warning radar system in Bahrain, marking the first reported strike against a Gulf country since early September. The US military’s Central Command (CENTCOM), which oversees American military operations in the region, said it shot down two Iranian drones targeting the Gulf island, adding that the attack caused no casualties or damage. item.title: Nigerian property owner in US named among worst landlords after building collapse kills eight
item.description: A Nigerian property owner, Olufemi Falade whose building collapsed onto an adjacent construction site in Brooklyn, New York, killing eight people, reportedly owes more than $450,000 in unpaid taxes, water bills and government fines. The property owner has also been listed six times on the New York City public advocate’s annual “Worst Landlords Watchlist” over allegations of poor property management. According to the New York Post, an examination of city records showed that Falade accumulated most of the outstanding debts through the three-storey building at 1321 Flatbush Avenue, which collapsed on Wednesday. The records indicated that he owes $170,000 in fines issued by the Department of Buildings in 2019 over improperly displayed signs, alongside $114,945 in unpaid water bills and $113,526 in property taxes dating back to 2021. Falade also reportedly owes the Internal Revenue Service $49,269 in unpaid personal federal income taxes, according to a 2010 lien, as well as another $4,316 in personal income taxes to New York State. The building, which had 98 outstanding violations with the city’s Department of Housing Preservation and Development before the collapse, reportedly had a history of maintenance and safety problems. The violations included a leaking roof, defective doors, bedbug infestations and exposed electrical wiring. Records showed that complaints over the leaking roof dated back to 1976, with further violations issued as recently as this year. Falade purchased the 96-year-old property in 1999 through an entity known as Femi Realty Corp. In November 2024, he transferred ownership to another company he controls, Isolag Realty Corp, signing the deed as both seller and buyer without any money changing hands. The report also revealed that Falade was sentenced to 12 days in jail in 2006 and fined $50,000 for civil contempt after failing to address more than 1,800 violations across 12 Brooklyn buildings he owned at the time. Meanwhile, questions have emerged over the approval of excavation plans at an adjacent construction site believed to have contributed to the collapse. The New York City Department of Buildings reportedly approved the excavation plans in March for a proposed three-storey, 25,000-square-foot mixed-use development at 2625 Bedford Avenue. However, the approved plans allegedly failed to provide adequate structural reinforcement alongside the building that subsequently collapsed. Real estate attorney Massimo D’Angelo, of Blank Rome, called for improved coordination between city agencies responsible for property safety and enforcement. item.title: US Thrash Haiti As Pochettino Prepares For Farewell
item.description: The United States thrashed Haiti 6-0 to surge towards the CONCACAF Nations League semi-finals on Saturday as Mauricio Pochettino’s penultimate game in charge ended in an emphatic victory. Goals from Christian Pulisic (2), Auston Trusty, Julian Hall, Weston McKennie and Folarin Balogun gave the US a commanding first-leg advantage to all but settle the outcome of the quarter-final before Tuesday’s second leg in Cincinnati. The build-up to Saturday’s fixture in Miami had been overshadowed by news of Pochettino’s departure as US coach after agreeing to take over Manchester United. But there was little sign that news of Pochettino’s exit had disturbed US preparations as they demolished World Cup qualifiers Haiti to deliver the biggest victory of the Argentine coach’s two-year reign. “Pochettino is an amazing manager, and he’s added a lot to us with the national team,” goalscorer Balogun said afterwards. “It’s always sad when you see a top coach leave, but it’s a part of the sport. “I think it was just important for us today to stick together and get the win — it just makes the send-off better,” Balogun added. Trusty gave the Americans the lead after just 10 minutes, confidently finishing from close range after Sebastian Berhalter’s free-kick from the right flank. Fans of Haiti cheer during the CONCACAF Nations League Quarterfinal match between Haiti and United States at Nu Stadium on November 14, 2026 in Miami, Florida. JC Ruiz/Getty Images/AFP (Photo by JC Ruiz / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP) That goal was all that separated the teams at half-time, but the floodgates opened after the break. Hall calmly tucked away Antonee Robinson’s low cross in the 52nd minute after a sweeping counter-attack to make it 2-0. Pulisic made it 3-0 from the penalty spot 10 minutes later after being brought down in the box by Haiti defender Carlens Arcus. The AC Milan forward then grabbed his second goal a minute later, rifling into the bottom corner from the edge of the area to make it 4-0. McKennie’s 68th-minute header put Pochettino’s side 5-0 up, and the US thought they had added a sixth soon afterwards when Balogun shrugged off Arcus to score from close range. Weston McKennie #8 of United States celebrates scoring his team’s fifth goal during the CONCACAF Nations League Quarterfinal match between Haiti and United States at Nu Stadium on November 14, 2026 in Miami.(Photo by JC Ruiz / GETTY IMAGES NORTH AMERICA / Getty Images via AFP) A VAR review, however, determined that Balogun had fouled Arcus in the build-up and the goal was chalked off. Balogun did not have long to wait, though, for his 13th international goal, latching on to a Malik Tillman through ball to score in the 82nd minute. item.title: CHINA DIARIES: The Future of farming
item.description: When we talk about China’s development, the images that often come to mind are high-speed trains, towering skyscrapers, electric vehicles and impressive infrastructure. But there is another quiet revolution taking place, one that is just as important to China’s future: agriculture. I had an opportunity to explore this during a visit to Yangling, in Shaanxi Province, a place that has become an important centre for agricultural science, research, innovation and technology. Our visit took us to three facilities: the SCO Demonstration Base for Agricultural Technology Exchange and Training, the Yangling Smart Agriculture Demonstration Park, and Yangling Liangke Agricultural Science and Technology Co. Ltd. What I saw offered an interesting glimpse into how China is using science and technology to rethink farming, improve productivity and strengthen food security. China Diaries: An Emperor, 8,000 Soldiers and a Lesson for Nigeria! 2027: We’ll fight Tinubu in South, North-Central, sweep North-West, North-East – Amaechi And, naturally, it got me thinking about Nigeria. Where farming meets the digital age One of the most interesting parts of the visit was seeing how technology is being integrated into everyday agricultural activities. At the smart agriculture demonstration facility, I saw a control station where plants are monitored through screens. Rather than relying entirely on physical observation, information about growing conditions can be monitored centrally, allowing operators to keep track of what is happening inside the growing facilities. It was a reminder that modern farming is increasingly becoming a data-driven activity. The farmer of the future may still walk through the farm, inspect the crops and get his hands dirty, but technology is giving him additional tools to make better decisions. I also saw vegetables being cultivated indoors in a controlled environment. It was fascinating to see food production taking place in a setting that looked quite different from the conventional farms we are familiar with in Nigeria. The idea is to manage growing conditions and create a more controlled environment for production. Such systems can help reduce dependence on some external weather conditions and make production more predictable, although their commercial viability depends on energy, infrastructure and operating costs. Another interesting sight was the display of grains and seedlings. These may look ordinary at first glance, but they represent an important part of the agricultural value chain: research, seed development and the effort to improve the quality and productivity of crops before they even get to the farm. Then came the agricultural drones. I photographed drones designed to spray farmland. Their use illustrates how technology can help farmers cover large areas more efficiently and apply agricultural treatments with greater precision. item.title: [VIDEO] ‘We’re The Only Party With 13 States,’ Amaechi Says ADC Will Win North-East, North-West
item.description: The vice-presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Rotimi Amaechi, has expressed confidence that the party will defeat the All Progressives Congress (APC) in the North East and North West. Speaking at a presidential rally in Bauchi State on Saturday, Amaechi said that while the ADC has the support of 13 northern states in the two regions, President Bola Tinubu of the APC has five in the South West, adding that the sixth state would vote for the Allied Peoples Movement, which has Governor Seyi Makinde as its presidential candidate. The former Rivers State governor said that the ADC would wipe out corruption, tackle insecurity, and make sure farmers can return to their farms. He also urged Nigerians to vote and protect their votes. Watch the video below.
